value.rationale: The isotropic constant is a natural affine-invariant high-dimensional measure. Exact all-layer covariance reduces an n-dimensional determinant to k dimensions, and sharp asymptotics identify a universal logarithmic deficit counted by the poset layer interfaces; this is motivated beyond a finite calculation and distinguishes the effect of ordinal-sum depth from layer imbalance. For two layers a complete exact determinant and its explicit limiting constant are obtained.
